summary.oneLiner: Manufacturer of aluminium alloy wheels for four-wheeler vehicles in India, part of Japan's Enkei Group.
summary.business: Enkei Wheels (India) Limited manufactures aluminium alloy wheels for four-wheeler (4W) vehicles in India, serving the domestic automotive industry as a component supplier. The Company is part of the Enkei Group, with Enkei Corporation, Japan as its holding company.

endMarkets: Indian domestic four-wheeler (passenger/other) automotive OEM market

currentContext.strengths: Emphasis on improving production by adopting advanced technologies, installing modern machinery and leveraging the technical expertise of its skilled workforce (SWOT: Strength).
currentContext.strategies: Continuously striving to improve the production process, aiming to reduce production time, minimise wastage and increase overall productivity.|Focusing on developing domestic sourcing capabilities for raw materials (alloy) to ensure a stable, uninterrupted supply chain.|Initiating towards obtaining a laser marking facility as part of R&D efforts.|Has started ISI marking inside the wheel as per BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) regulation and customer requirement.|Continuous energy-conservation practices at factories (e.g. reducing furnace door opening gap, stopping burners during alloy pouring, common compressor connections) to reduce energy consumption while maximising production volumes.|Directors did not recommend payment of dividend for FY2025, citing capital retention for the Company's future business expansion and diversification plan; the AGM notice also sought a special resolution to raise the Board's borrowing limit under Section 180(1)(c) up to an aggregate of INR 500 crore.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025, the Company completed the upgradation of the MAP 2 facility into the MAT facility, described as the most advanced technical process, which reduces the manufacturing time of 4W wheels; this MAP2 facility will increase production capacity by around 20,000 pieces per month. The Company has also established a new production unit, MAC 5, at its Factory 2 location, which along with the MAP2-to-MAT conversion has enhanced overall production capacity, reduced manufacturing lead times and improved product quality. The Company continues to strive to improve its production process, aiming to reduce production time, minimise wastage and increase overall productivity.
currentContext.mdna: Passenger vehicle segment likely to witness steady growth, led by customer preference for SUVs and feature-rich models, supporting demand across urban and semi-urban markets.|Commercial vehicle segment anticipated to improve gradually owing to infrastructure spending, logistics expansion and construction activity.|Two-wheeler segment expected to remain resilient, supported by rural income, financing access and cost-efficient models.|Structural shift toward electric mobility and cleaner technologies; EV adoption continues to expand with sales reaching nearly a 20% rise in total volume.|Increasing consumer preference for electric vehicles and advanced vehicle components such as alloy wheels reflects positive industry trends for the Company's product category.|Growth opportunities from consistent government support via PLI scheme, Make in India, Ease of Doing Business and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives promoting domestic manufacturing and MSMEs.|Weakness/threat: high energy and labour costs, along with rising raw material prices, remain key constraints and may increase operating expenses and working capital interest costs; a significant increase in raw material/energy costs or economic slowdowns in domestic and global markets may pose challenges to growth.

risks.risk: Long-term growth dependent on further capacity expansion (Strategic Risk)
risks.note: Capacity utilisation across all plants is steadily increasing; as the business environment improves, long-term growth is expected to depend on further capacity expansion beyond the recently added MAC 5 unit and MAP2-to-MAT conversion.
Alloy, the primary raw material, accounts for around 55-60% of the Company's overall cost structure, exposing it to supply disruptions and volatility in market prices.

Employee engagement and productivity are crucial to growth; loss of skilled talent through attrition may affect the Company's growth given the need for creativity, innovative thinking and cross-domain expertise.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates may expose the Company to transaction and translation risks; monitored quarterly by the Audit Committee.
High-level outstanding debt, particularly during challenging economic conditions, could adversely affect the Company's financial flexibility and business performance.
Customer defaults may pose a significant risk and adversely impact the Company's financial performance.
The Company is governed by various regulations and contractual obligations; any non-compliance may adversely affect its performance.

Rapid expansion of the automotive industry raises concerns around intellectual property protection, data privacy and warranty-related risk allocation, alongside risks such as cyber-attacks, hacking and internal data leakage.
